text: Ten fictional nonprofit programme passages, each with eight quote variants (exact, whitespace/case, punctuation, changed quantity, added negation, removed negation, reordered, paraphrase) for citation-checker testing.

passages.source_passage: The mid-term evaluation of the Kalembe Village Savings Initiative covered 42 savings groups across Nyandeni and Lusoro wards between March and June 2023. Members had saved a combined total of 1.8 million shillings, and 76 percent of groups had completed at least one full share-out cycle. Loan repayment rates remained high, with fewer than three groups reporting overdue balances. However, the evaluators found that record books were not updated consistently in a third of the groups visited. Women made up most of the membership, and group chairs reported that members used loans mainly for school fees and small livestock. The team did not observe any group that had dissolved since the baseline survey. Field officers recommended refresher training on bookkeeping before the second cycle begins in January.

passages.source_passage: Merati District in the western highlands has a population of roughly 310,000 people served by only 14 health facilities, most of them clustered along the main road. Since 2019, the Tumaini Health Partnership has trained and deployed 260 community health workers to visit households in the outlying sub-counties. Each worker covers about 120 households and refers pregnant women, sick children and suspected tuberculosis cases to the nearest clinic. Despite this progress, workers are not paid a regular stipend, and attrition reached 18 percent in the last financial year. Many workers walk more than ten kilometres between villages and have no bicycles or reliable phones. The district health office has never had a dedicated budget line for community health. This proposal requests funding to stabilise the cadre and extend coverage to two additional sub-counties.

variants.removed_negation: The district health office has had a dedicated budget line for community health.
variants.reordered: This proposal requests funding to stabilise coverage and extend the cadre to two additional sub-counties.
variants.paraphrase: Last year 18 percent of the health workers, who receive no regular stipend, left the programme.

passages.source_passage: Before each home visit, volunteers should review the referral form and confirm which assistive device the client has been assessed for. In the Sereno Mobility Project, most clients receive either a walking frame or a wheelchair, and about 1 in 5 also need a cushion fitted on the same day. Do not adjust a wheelchair without first asking the user how they prefer to sit and transfer. Allow at least 45 minutes for a first fitting, because rushed sessions often lead to devices being abandoned. Remember that the person using the device is the expert on their own body; the volunteer is not. After the visit, record the device serial number and arrange a follow-up check within two weeks. Volunteers should never promise ramps or home modifications that the project has not approved.

passages.source_passage: At the mid-point of the project, the Anandpur Mother and Child Outreach team had reached 3,400 pregnant women through monthly clinic days in 28 villages. Antenatal attendance of four or more visits rose from 41 percent at baseline to 63 percent by September 2022. Outreach nurses reported that home deliveries declined, but the evaluation could not confirm this because facility birth registers were incomplete. Newborn weighing was introduced in all sites, although scales were not available in six villages until the second quarter. Mothers interviewed in focus groups valued the clinic days and said they no longer had to travel to the district hospital for routine checks. The evaluation recommends extending postnatal visits to cover the first 42 days after birth.

passages.source_passage: During the 2023 season, the Green Furrow Farmer Field School network expanded from 54 to 71 schools across Kasiri and Mbeleko provinces. Around 2,100 smallholders, 58 percent of them women, attended weekly sessions on soil cover, seed selection and pest scouting. Participating farmers reported average maize yields of 2.4 tonnes per hectare, compared with 1.6 tonnes among neighbouring non-members. Rainfall was well below average in February, and the network did not meet its target for establishing seed banks. Facilitators noted that farmers who adopted mulching lost fewer crops during the dry spell. We have not yet secured an off-taker agreement for surplus beans, which remains a priority for next year. We thank the Foundation for its continued support.

passages.source_passage: Volunteers supporting the Haven Bridge Family Tracing Service must complete the two-day induction before meeting any child. When a child is first placed with a foster family, a caseworker visits within 72 hours and then every fortnight for the first three months. Volunteers do not conduct tracing interviews alone; they always accompany a trained caseworker. If a child mentions a relative's name or village, write it down exactly as spoken and pass it to the caseworker the same day. Never share a child's photograph on social media, even with the foster family's permission. Last year, 64 percent of traced families were reunified within six months, and none of those placements broke down. Patience matters more than speed in this work.

passages.source_passage: This update summarises progress in the Puentes de Futuro scholarship programme for the first semester of 2024. The programme currently supports 186 girls in lower and upper secondary schools across the departments of San Ilario and Valle Hondo. Attendance among scholars averaged 92 percent, and only four girls left school during the semester, two of them because of family migration. Staff have not been able to recruit a mentor for the Valle Hondo cohort since the previous coordinator resigned in February. The board approved a stipend increase last year, but transport costs have risen faster than expected. Exam results were not yet available at the time of writing. Management asks the board to consider a one-time transport grant for scholars in remote communities.

passages.source_passage: In the peri-urban settlements around Lomara, an estimated 9,000 children under five have no access to any form of organised early learning. Since 2021, the Little Steps Playgroup Network has established 35 community playgroups, each meeting three mornings a week in churches, homes and market halls. Playgroups are led by trained parent facilitators and focus on language, play and responsive caregiving. A 2023 assessment found that children attending for at least six months scored 22 percent higher on school-readiness measures than non-attending peers. Demand far exceeds capacity, and most playgroups now keep waiting lists. The network does not charge fees, and it has never turned away a child with a disability. Additional funding would allow us to open 20 new groups and train a further 60 facilitators.

passages.source_passage: Each Ubuntu Care volunteer is assigned between eight and twelve households and should visit every client at least once a week. During a visit, check whether the client has taken their antiretroviral medication and note any missed doses on the green card. Do not ask clients to show their pill bottles in front of visitors or neighbours. If a client has missed more than three doses in a month, inform the nurse supervisor within 24 hours. Volunteers are not expected to give injections or change wound dressings that require sterile equipment. Wear gloves when handling body fluids, and wash your hands before and after every visit. In 2022, volunteers made over 14,000 home visits, and no volunteer reported a needle-stick injury.

passages.source_passage: Volunteer listeners at the Safe Harbour Community Counselling Service offer up to six sessions to each client, usually lasting 50 minutes. Your role is to listen, reflect feelings and help the client identify sources of support; you are not a therapist and should not offer a diagnosis. In our 2023 review, 70 percent of clients said they felt heard during the first session. If a client talks about wanting to end their life, stay with them and contact the duty supervisor immediately. Never promise complete confidentiality, because safety concerns must be shared. Volunteers should attend group supervision every two weeks and keep brief notes after each session. Looking after your own wellbeing is part of the job, not an extra.
